metadata.notes: The fourth SALT-shaped seasoning verb — closed 2026-08-15, triaged from a user-supplied Reddit thread (olddocs/reddit-thread-1mo4tj8.md) naming 'Salt, Fat, Acid, Heat' as the single most-repeated organizing idea for cooking without recipes; Salt/Fat/Heat were already real, structural parts of this vocabulary, Acid had nothing until vinegar.json/this action. Same shape as salt.json/pepper.json/chili.json on purpose (outputs.addsTag not transformedState, same requiredTargetCapability, same timing parameter), deliberately NOT generalized into one parameter-driven SEASON verb, for the identical already-documented reason those three weren't (see pepper.json's notes — ActionOutputsSchema.addsTag has no addsTagFromParameter counterpart, and requiredIngredientCapabilities only checks presence, never identifies WHICH instance satisfied it). Acid's flavor role is chemically and perceptually distinct from salt's (osmosis/browning), pepper's (piperine pungency), and chili's (capsaicin pungency) — see src/flavor-balance.ts for the real, cited counterbalance data (acid perceptually cutting through richness, and its own sourness mutually suppressing/being suppressed by sweetness) this action's real-world effect actually traces to. Wired to potato.json/egg.json/egg_cracked.json only — the exact same footprint pepper.json/chili.json already have, not garlic.json — matching their own established 'capable, not forced into an existing dish that wasn't asked to have it' discipline rather than a new decision.
metadata.timingNote: Acid's real technique timing differs from salt's and from pepper/chili's aromatic-degradation concern: acid added too early to a long-simmering dish has more time to dull chlorophyll in green vegetables (a real, commonly-cited effect — acid accelerates the conversion of bright green chlorophyll to dull olive-green pheophytin) and can prevent a good sear/Maillard browning if splashed onto food before it hits a hot pan (the same 'moisture blocks browning until it's driven off' physics u/BattleHall's toaster explanation in the triaged Reddit thread names, generalized). Acid added at the very end (a finishing squeeze of citrus, a splash of vinegar off the heat) is the far more common real technique for the 'brightening'/richness-cutting effect this verb primarily exists to represent. Purely informational here, same limits as every other timing-style parameter in this vocabulary — this records what was asked for, it does not make the target's outcome depend on it.

verification.description: No reliable sensor check for 'properly acidified' in this vocabulary — taste isn't modeled at all
